product_scope.problem_statement: The core flow from phase 1 can dispatch and process provider work items, but it still lacks explicit operational resilience. The system needs to distinguish retryable failures from terminal failures, prevent duplicate processing, and reflect operational state transitions in a controlled way.
product_scope.goal: Extend the validated core orchestration flow with resilience, idempotency, and operational lifecycle control while preserving per-provider isolation and final outcome auditability.
success_outcomes: Retryable failures are retried before final closure.
Terminal failures stop retrying and close deterministically.
The same logical work item is not processed twice as an independent execution.
Pending work items expose a basic operational lifecycle in the system.
The system preserves enough evidence to understand how a work item progressed and why it finished the way it did.

in_scope: Explicit handling of retryable versus terminal provider failures.
Operational prevention of duplicate processing for the same logical work item.
Basic lifecycle states for pending work items.
Operational closure for successful, terminal, and exhausted retry outcomes.
Retention of per-provider serialization while resilience behavior is introduced.
Traceability of work-item progression through the operational flow.
out_of_scope: Advanced observability dashboards and metrics programs.
Full replay tooling or operator UI.

actors.name: Scheduler
actors.description: Starts the daily workload as in phase 1.

actors.name: Dispatch Flow
actors.description: Publishes eligible work items for downstream execution.

actors.name: Operational Orchestration Flow
actors.description: Coordinates retries, failure closure, duplicate protection, and execution state progression.

actors.name: Provider API
actors.description: Returns successful, retryable, or terminal outcomes to a work item execution.

actors.name: Technical Reviewer
actors.description: Needs to verify that resilience and operational guarantees are explicitly modeled.

user_journeys.name: Retryable failure is retried before closure
steps: A pending work item is dispatched and starts execution.
The provider responds with a retryable failure.
The system recognizes that the work item should be retried.
The system retries the execution according to operational policy.
The work item eventually succeeds or reaches a final exhausted state.

user_journeys.name: Terminal failure closes deterministically
steps: A pending work item starts execution.
The provider responds with a terminal failure.
The system recognizes that retrying would not resolve the problem.
The system records the terminal outcome and closes the work item.

user_journeys.name: Duplicate execution is blocked
steps: A logical work item enters the operational flow.
A duplicate instance of the same logical work item appears before the original is fully resolved or after it has already completed.
The system identifies that both instances refer to the same logical work item.
The duplicate instance is prevented from producing an independent second execution outcome.

user_journeys.name: Pending record lifecycle becomes visible
steps: A pending record starts in a pending state.
The system marks it as actively being processed.
The system closes it as completed or failed depending on the final outcome.
A reviewer can inspect the record state and understand its operational status.

use_cases.title: Retry a retryable provider failure
use_cases.description: The system retries a provider request when the failure is considered temporary or safe to repeat.

use_cases.title: Close a terminal provider failure
use_cases.description: The system stops retrying and records the outcome when the failure is definitively not recoverable through repetition.

use_cases.title: Prevent duplicate work-item processing
use_cases.description: The system blocks a second operational execution for the same logical work item.

use_cases.title: Reflect processing lifecycle on pending records
use_cases.description: The system updates the work-item lifecycle as it moves through processing.

use_cases.title: Preserve final auditability
use_cases.description: The system preserves final success and failure evidence after operational handling is complete.

business_rules.rule: A logical work item is uniquely identified by its business identity and execution date, and must not produce independent duplicate processing.
Retryable failures and terminal failures must lead to different operational outcomes.
A retryable failure may be attempted again before the work item is finally closed.
A terminal failure must stop retrying and close the work item deterministically.
Pending records must expose a minimum lifecycle that distinguishes not started, in progress, completed, and failed work.
A work item must preserve strict execution serialization within the same provider even while resilience behavior is added.
A work item may still execute in parallel with work items from different providers.
The final outcome history must remain available even when a work item is retried or blocked as duplicate.
Operational state progression must reflect the actual work status in the system, not only the raw provider response.
This phase prioritizes resilience and control of the existing core flow, not large-scale redesign.

functional_requirements.title: Retry classification
functional_requirements.statement: The system must distinguish retryable failures from terminal failures.

functional_requirements.title: Retry behavior
functional_requirements.statement: The system must retry a work item when the failure is classified as retryable.

functional_requirements.title: Terminal closure
functional_requirements.statement: The system must stop retrying and close the work item when the failure is classified as terminal.

functional_requirements.title: Duplicate protection
functional_requirements.statement: The system must prevent the same logical work item from being processed twice as an independent execution.

functional_requirements.title: Pending lifecycle visibility
functional_requirements.statement: The system must expose a basic operational lifecycle for pending records.

functional_requirements.title: Success closure
functional_requirements.statement: The system must mark and preserve a successful operational completion.

functional_requirements.title: Failure closure
functional_requirements.statement: The system must mark and preserve a failed operational completion when retries are exhausted or the failure is terminal.

functional_requirements.title: Operational traceability
functional_requirements.statement: The system must leave enough evidence to explain how a work item progressed, retried, completed, failed, or was blocked as duplicate.

functional_requirements.title: Provider isolation preservation
functional_requirements.statement: The system must preserve same-provider serialization while applying resilience rules.

functional_requirements.title: Cross-provider parallelism preservation
functional_requirements.statement: The system must continue allowing progress across different providers at the same time.

interaction_expectations.expectation: A reviewer should be able to understand why a work item was retried, closed as terminal, or blocked as duplicate.
The operational lifecycle of a pending record should make the system easier to reason about during debugging and review.
The resilience layer should feel like an extension of the core flow, not a contradictory second model.

acceptance_criteria.given: A work item fails with a retryable outcome
acceptance_criteria.then: The system retries the work item before deciding its final closure.

acceptance_criteria.given: A work item fails with a terminal outcome
acceptance_criteria.then: The system stops retrying and closes the work item as failed.

acceptance_criteria.given: A retryable work item exhausts its allowed attempts
acceptance_criteria.when: The operational flow finishes handling it
acceptance_criteria.then: The system closes the work item as a final failed outcome.

acceptance_criteria.given: The same logical work item appears more than once
acceptance_criteria.when: The operational flow receives the duplicate instance
acceptance_criteria.then: The system prevents a second independent processing outcome from being produced.

acceptance_criteria.when: The operational flow starts work on it
acceptance_criteria.then: The record is reflected as in progress.
The pending record is reflected as completed and the final success outcome remains persisted.

acceptance_criteria.given: A work item finishes as terminal or exhausted failure
acceptance_criteria.then: The pending record is reflected as failed and the final failure outcome remains persisted.

acceptance_criteria.given: Two or more work items belong to the same provider
acceptance_criteria.then: The system still processes them one at a time and in order.

acceptance_criteria.given: Work items belong to different providers
acceptance_criteria.then: The system may still progress them in parallel.

acceptance_criteria.given: A technical reviewer inspects a processed work item
acceptance_criteria.when: They review logs, states, and persisted outcomes
acceptance_criteria.then: They can understand whether it succeeded, failed terminally, exhausted retries, or was blocked as duplicate.

assumptions: Phase 1 established the core flow and remains the foundation for this phase.
The logical identity of a work item is stable enough to support duplicate protection.
The challenge benefits from making operational state explicit even before large-scale redesign is addressed.
Retry policy details belong to the technical spec, while retry versus terminal behavior belongs to this functional spec.

open_questions.question: What exact business identity should be treated as the canonical duplicate-protection key if future requirements introduce more than recordId plus scheduledDate?
Should duplicate work items be visible to operators as a special closed state, or is it sufficient for them to be blocked without a distinct business-facing status?
